transport: RJ45 RS-485 to 2.4 GHz WiFi (2.4–2.4835 GHz) · serial side 115200 bps 8N1 · vendor calls the interface standard 'EPEVER communication standard V1-1.0', not Modbus · powered 5 V ±0.5 V from the RS-485 comms port, peak emission 150 mA, idle 310 µA · RJ45 pins 1,2 = +5VDC · 3,4 = RS485-B · 5,6 = RS485-A · 7,8 = GND

gotchas: THE BLOCKING FACT: the vendor manual names two working modes — 'Local monitoring' and 'EPEVER Cloud' — and states NO TCP port, NO listening service, NO framing, and NO register access for either. The only documented client is the Solar Guardian phone app. Nothing about a gateway reading this adapter is vendor-documente

EPEver support, quoted by a Home Assistant user who owns this exact model on a Tracer 1206AN: 'their dongle only supports the mobile phone app.' The same user's port scan of the D found only 80 and 8899 open, and an attempt to speak Modbus on 8899 returned 'No response received, expected at least 8 bytes (0 received)'.

CONTRADICTION, recorded not resolved. A second Home Assistant poster reports a working `type: rtuovertcp`, `port: 9999`, `slave: 10` against a UPower-Hi behind a D adapter. But port 9999 with a browser config page at http://<ip>/ offering 'Protocol = TCP-Server, Port ID = 9999' is the signature of a third-party Elfin E

A third, different route exists: the D dials OUT to hncomm.epsolarpv.com:15000 as a client. One developer redirected that hostname to a local Python server, sent an init sequence `20020000` after each adapter restart, and then spoke RTU-over-TCP over the hijacked connection. `community-single`.
